key_insight: Fixed orthogonalized momentum can fail on nonsmooth convex optimization, but making momentum adaptive and combining it with gradients restores reliable convergence.
engineering_relevance: For matrix-valued models in deep learning and pretraining, MAGD offers a geometry-aware optimizer that is practical, dimension-efficient, and more robust than Muon on nonsmooth objectives.
method: Analyze Muon under locally Lipschitz nonsmooth optimization using generalized derivatives.
Show a failure case for any fixed momentum factor beta in convex Lipschitz problems, even with bounded iterates.
Propose MAGD, which blends orthogonalized momentum with gradient weighting and adaptive momentum approaching 1.
evidence_signal: The paper reports synthetic experiments, image classification, and LLM pretraining results, alongside theoretical asymptotic convergence and an O(min{m,n} eps^-2) convex rate.
watch_item: Performance depends on adaptive schedules and regularity/boundedness assumptions, so fixed-momentum Muon may still be unreliable in practice on nonsmooth tasks.
